scientific_findings: Frame equations are correct for one shared center and anchor. Native topocentric-air wavelengths convert to barycentric once, then merged/native profiles use the same requested frame grid. Both discovery references are resampled on this common grid, without event-specific recentering.

The useful addition is core-versus-surrounding-pattern context against both discovery references. Signed flux remains intact; there is no fitted continuum, line, width, lag, center or drift optimization. Raw Pearson and normalized RMS are descriptive shape metrics.

Per-profile/per-frame normalization uses a signed pooled flank median, requiring at least20 finite native samples separately in each fixed flank and a positive pooled median. Missing, insufficient and nonpositive reference cases remain distinct and raw-only. Noise pairs stay within one flank and do not bridge gaps.

Native order3 lacks the left broad-window normalization flank by header geometry. Raw-only status here means missing coverage, distinct from historically low/nonpositive local continuum. A finite raw-core Pearson can still occur; it must not be called independent corroboration. No extrapolation or smaller window is introduced.

Native flux units are explicitly unspecified while merged ADU is verified. Native-to-merged normalized RMS is separate-scaling shape context, not physical flux ratio. Positive scalar normalization alone does not change Pearson correlation.

All six merged epochs, four native order/exposure combinations and four historical raw panels remain present, with self/shared-exposure flags and failed slots retained. Geometry support and native signal usefulness remain separate; historical mapping/epoch values and U labels are untouched.
Plot rules retain signed values, raw-only annotations and unit labels; frame limits are shared where declared and separate raw-panel scales are disclosed. Full fixed windows are preserved.

Final prospective corrections replace exact-zero standard-deviation testing with a peak-to-peak constant-array guard and fail closed on selected flux/error shape mismatch. These correct numerical validity checks without changing frames, normalization, windows or estimators.
